Punch Trainer: Target Dummy Combat

Proposal approved · revision 2

Mechanics

Core loop: the player walks up to a stationary target dummy and presses an attack input (left mouse click or a designated attack key) to throw a punch. On input, the player's Humanoid plays the punch animation once; this happens regardless of range so the action always feels responsive. A short-range hit check (proximity/region check in front of the player, or a touch-based hit zone on the dummy) determines whether the punch lands. If the player is within punching range of the dummy when the swing's 'impact point' occurs, it counts as a successful hit: the punch/hit sound plays at the dummy's location, and an on-screen counter (a GUI TextLabel, e.g. 'Hits: 0') increments by one. If the player swings while out of range, the animation still plays but no sound is played and the counter does not increment (a whiff). A short cooldown/debounce between successful hit registrations prevents a single animation from double-counting or the player from spamming clicks to inflate the counter unrealistically. The dummy itself is purely a target: it does not take damage, does not have health, and does not fall over or reset — its role is solely to be the object the player aims at. The counter is per-player, visible at all times during play, and persists only for the current session (resets to 0 on join/respawn) unless otherwise specified. There is no win/lose condition; this is a practice/combo-drill style loop focused on the punch-hit-count feedback cycle.

Assumptions: Single-player experience (or each player sees/tracks only their own counter) since no multiplayer scoring/competition was requested. Attack input defaults to left mouse click on PC, with touch/tap support assumed for mobile; no combo or special-move inputs are included. Hit detection uses a simple range/proximity check in front of the player rather than precise hitbox-vs-hitbox collision, since no combat depth beyond 'punch the dummy' was requested. The dummy has no health, damage, ragdoll, or defeat state — it is a permanent, indestructible training target. A brief per-swing cooldown (roughly matching animation length) prevents multiple counter increments from one punch. The on-screen counter resets to zero when a player joins or respawns; no persistent cross-session leaderboard is implied. Only one target dummy is needed; the player always punches the same fixed dummy rather than multiple targets.

Theme

A minimal boxing/martial-arts training theme: the experience is framed as a personal training session rather than a competitive fighting game. Visual language leans into a gym or dojo aesthetic — plain, functional, and focused on making the punch-and-counter feedback the star rather than elaborate combat systems or storyline. No enemies, no narrative, no progression tiers beyond the hit counter itself; the tone is practice-drill, arcade-style skill-building.

Assumptions: No narrative framing, factions, or cosmetic customization is implied since the request is purely mechanical (punch, sound, counter). Visual style defaults to a simple, clean gym/training aesthetic rather than a stylized cartoon or realistic fighting-game art direction, since none was specified.

Environment & layout

A small, self-contained training area: a flat rectangular platform (roughly 20x20 studs) serving as the practice floor, with the target dummy fixed near the center-front of the space (approx. position [0,3,10]) so the player has a clear approach path and unobstructed view of the on-screen counter. A single player spawn point is placed a short distance from the dummy (e.g., 10-12 studs back) so the player must walk up to punching range rather than starting adjacent to it. Basic even lighting (default baseplate-style lighting) is sufficient since atmosphere is not the focus. No additional obstacles, other NPCs, or secondary rooms are needed — the layout should stay simple and uncluttered so the punch-and-counter loop is the sole focus of the space.

Assumptions: A single flat platform area is sufficient; no multi-room gym or additional training equipment is required since only one dummy interaction was requested. Default Roblox baseplate-style lighting and skybox are acceptable since no specific atmosphere or time-of-day was requested. Only one spawn point and one dummy are needed; the layout does not need to scale to multiple simultaneous players punching separate dummies unless later requested.
